CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION, OTTAWA, December 27, 1923.

Re: Compensation for the Class "Inspector of Construction"

DEAR SIR, - With reference to your letter of the 21st instant inquiring as to the opinion of the Commissioners
regarding the daily rate of pay for the above class, I am directed to inform you that your understanding of the matter
coincides with that of the Commissioners, i.e., that a man appointed to a position in this class at a daily rate is entitled
to pay only for those days on which he is actually engaged on inspection work.

Yours truly,
W. FORAN, Secretary.

Assistant A.G.

Disposal of Stock and Equipment, Dunbow (St. Joseph's) Industrial School

AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, March 27, 1923.

SIR, - I understand that the Dunbow Indian Industrial School, near High River, Alberta, was recently closed, and that
the stock and equipment was disposed of by one of your inspectors. Kindly let me have a copy of any report that may
have been made by your inspector with regard to the disposal of the assets of this school, giving the amount realized
from the sale with the disposal of the resulting funds, and also what part, if any, of the stock and equipment was
disposed of otherwise than by sale.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, OTTAWA, April 4, 1923.

DEAR MR. KEARNS, - I have your letter of the 27th ultimo, with reference to the closing of the Dunbow Indian
Industrial School in Alberta.

In reply I have to state that the transaction has not yet been completed, and, when it comes before you for audit, I shall
be pleased to offer you, as usual, any information you require.

Yours very truly,
DUNCAN C. SCOTT, Deputy Supt. General.

The Assistant Auditor General, Ottawa.

AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, December 28, 1923.

SIR, - On March 27th last I wrote you with reference to the closing of the Dunbow Industrial School, asking for a
copy of any report with regard to the disposal of the assets of that school, made by your inspector who disposed of the
stock and equipment. In your reply of April 4th you stated that the transaction had not yet been completed, but that
when it came before me for audit you would supply me with such information as I might require.

I find that in December, 1922, the amount of $6,026.79 was remitted by Mr. Graham, representing the balance of the
proceeds arising from the disposal of the stock and equipment, which amount was placed to the credit of Trust
Account. No. 449. Against this deposit the following cheques were drawn on March 31st: -

8399 Rev. Mother Provincial Grey Nuns $1,225 18
8402 Rev. Provincial Oblate Fathers     4,324 19
8400 Receiver General, to close account 477 42

As this account is now officially before me for audit, I have to renew my request for a copy of your inspector's report
relating to this matter.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

Advances on account of Grant to Lytton Industrial School

AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, December 7th, 1923.

SIR, - I beg to ask your attention to the payments made during the fiscal year 1922 - 23 to Rev. A.R. Lett, principal of
the Lytton Industrial School, on account of the per capita grant to that Institution.

The grant allowed your department for this school is at the rate of $195 per capita per annum, the payments being
based on the average attendance each

<!-- page 608 -->
quarter. The grant was at first allowed for a maximum of 100 pupils but that maximum was later on increased to 105
pupils. The payments in question are as follows: -

Cheque No. 2, April 6, 1922, Advance for June quarter                                                         $3,000 00
Cheque No. 150, April 26, 1922, Further advance for June qr.                                                  4,000 00
Cheque No. 1079, July 13, 1922, Grant for June quarter (100 pupils)                                           4,875 00
Cheque No. 2347, Oct. 16, 1922, Grant for Sept. quarter (Average 91.78) $4,474.27 less one-half
                                                                                                              974 27
advances, $3,500
Cheque No. 2176, Nov. 3, 1922, Advance for December quarter                                                   2,000 00
Cheque No. 4106, Jan. 19, 1923, Grant for December quarter (average 101.91) less balance of advances
                                                                                                              1,467 52
for June quarter, $3,500
Cheque No. 4106, Jan. 19, 1923, Balance of grant for June quarter (average 101.92)                            93 50
Cheque No. 4641, Feb. 26, 1923, Advance for March quarter                                                     1,500 00
Cheque No. 4922, March 20, 1923, Further advance for March quarter                                            1,200 00

While it is true that the total payments for the year do not exceed the earnings of the school, I should like an
explanation of the circumstances under which the various advances were made, especially the advances on account of
the June quarter, $7,000 in all having been advanced during that quarter, when the total earnings for that period were
only $4,875, and in addition to these advances of $7,000, the full amount of the quarterly grant was paid shortly after
the termination of the quarter.

While I understand that it may occasionally be necessary to make advances to a residential school before the end of the
quarter, I am of opinion that any advances so made should not exceed the probable amount of the earnings of the
school up to the date on which the advance is made.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, OTTAWA, July 10, 1923.

DEAR MR. KEARNS, - I have your letter of the 27th ultimo, with reference to certain payments made by this
Department in connection with the Squamish Indian Boarding School in North Vancouver.

In reply I wish to state that this school is situated within the Municipality of North Vancouver, on property not owned
by the Government. It is maintained by a per capita grant, paid from Parliamentary appropriation. Representations
were made to the Department that owing to the situation of the school the financial aid so derived was inadequate. I
decided, therefore, to relieve them of taxation, which would place this school in the same position as an institution
located on an Indian reserve. We therefore purchased Block 123, District Lot 271, North Vancouver, from the
Reverend Sisters, and as it is now Government property, it is non-taxable, and we have assumed the payment of the
taxes on Lot 69, on which the school buildings are situated.

Yours very truly,
DUNCAN C. SCOTT, Deputy Supt. General.

The Assistant Auditor General, Ottawa.
